text:
A: Hello. Can you see me? The angle's a bit odd, it's on the island.
B: Yes, I can see you fine. Hi, I'm Laura.
A: Gillian. Erm, do you actually know what this is all for? They didn't really say.
B: Not really, no. Something about first impressions, I think. How people get on.
A: Right. Well. As long as nobody's selling my details, that's all I care about.
B: Ha, yeah. So where are you based?
A: Bramhall. Stockport, sort of South Manchester. It's a nice area. You?
B: Basingstoke. Chineham, on the edge of it.
A: Oh, I don't know it. Is it nice?
B: It's fine. It's an estate, but it's quiet. Lakes nearby, that kind of thing.
A: Mm. And what do you do?
B: I'm a management accountant. Logistics company, I do the monthly figures for three depots.
A: Oh, right. I'm an optometrist. Three days a week, in Stockport town centre.
B: Oh, okay. So eye tests and that?
A: Eye tests, eye health, referrals if something's not right. Which is fine, that's the job, I don't mind that bit. It's everything else. They've got targets now for selling glasses, add-ons, coatings, and the manager stands there watching while you're trying to talk someone through a cataract. And parking in Stockport is a nightmare, so I'm already wound up by the time I get in. I'm shattered after a Tuesday, honestly. Erm, yeah, that's it really.
B: I can imagine. We've got targets too, but they're more cost ones. I'm usually the one telling people their numbers don't add up.
A: I bet that makes you popular.
B: Ha, not massively. I try to just quietly fix it, to be honest.
A: Sensible. Have you got kids?
B: One, Alfie. He's six. He's just started swimming lessons on a Tuesday, so that's my Tuesday gone as well.
A: Oh, I remember all that. Mine are grown up now. Son's in Leeds, daughter's at uni in Nottingham. She rings when she needs money, which is most weeks.
B: Is it quiet with them both gone?
A: Erm... it's quieter. We've got the dog, so. Bella. She's down there somewhere. She needs her nails doing and the groomer wants forty-five pound, which is daylight robbery.
B: Forty-five? For nails?
A: For a full groom. But still. I'm not paying it just for her nails, do you know what I mean?
B: No, fair enough. We've got a cat, he just gets fat and is sick on the rug.
A: Ha. Lovely.
B: Erm, so what do you do on your days off?
A: Walk Bella round the park. Pool and sauna at the gym. Telly. Married at First Sight with a glass of wine, I'm not going to pretend otherwise.
B: Ha, I watch Bake Off. And Gogglebox.
A: Oh, Gogglebox is good. Martin, my husband, hates it, so I put it on while I'm doing tea.
B: Tea as in dinner?
A: Yeah, tea. Half six. Sorry, northern.
B: No, it's fine. I'm dinner. My nan said tea, actually.
A: There you go. Your nan had it right.
B: Maybe. Erm, do you get away much?
A: Algarve most summers, same villa complex. I don't like flying, so I go where I know. Last time we did Rome, five-star, lovely hotel.
B: We're the same, really. Cornwall three years running. I like to know what I'm getting.
A: Exactly. People think it's boring. It's not boring, it's just—
